scope: Four native games through the whole launcher: two teams battle 2v2 from the Players menu with full parties (six Pokemon per trainer, twelve a side; the owner's rule). Four real launcher workers (LauncherWindow, SessionWorker, LauncherSession; host and three friends) start four native games from a native runtime bundle; production world creation, host enrollment of the four legacy saves through bootstrap games (each walks out of Route 101's grass into Littleroot first), the friends' invitations; ordinary team invitations and acceptances form two duos; the host challenges the other team to 2v2, the other three accept, all four press Enter battle; default moves and forced switches until the battle ends; all four launchers report battle_finished with their original games, bridges and runtime identities; the durable result is the same for all four; each player's exact personal party is back in memory; each game's Recent battle results shows it; all four save (revision 2), close normally (friends first) and Continue again onto the same canonical saves; the host store passes its integrity check; source saves unchanged. Ordinary key presses on each player's own X display; the harness reads the games' memory only to see menus, tasks and parties.

runs.clients: Linux i386 native client x4 (engine claude/native-pc 1579e7fd8: the battle branch's crash fixes, XInput at run time), started by the launchers' session workers; 640x360 windows (windowScale=2) and SDL_FRAMEBUFFER_ACCELERATION=0 so four games share the cloud computer's two cores
checks: each of the four sources walked out of Route 101's grass into its own spot in Littleroot (25-27 steps, direction keys checked step by step) and was enrolled through its bootstrap game (exit 0), revision 1, parties unchanged (six each)
four launchers started their games in Littleroot; ordinary team invitations formed two exact duos (accounts 0+1, 2+3)
challenge 2v2 from the host's Your team; the three others accepted; four identical consent descriptors; all four pressed Enter battle

the battle ran to its end on the host's battle service: 5545 routed blocks in 8391.6 s; seventeen party selections, the sixth Pokemon (slot 5) sent out by three trainers; the host's second Pokemon selected
all four launchers report battle_finished with the original game processes, runtime objects, bridges and runtime identities; no battle ownership or pending recovery intent left
the durable result is the same for all four (mode 3: 2v2, team 1 won, sequence 1)
each player's full personal party restored in memory; each game's Recent battle results shows 'Team 1 won'
all four saved through the launcher (revision 2); all four games closed normally (exit 0 x4)
fresh launchers Continued all four onto the same canonical checkpoints (revision 2, the same parties); closed normally (exit 0 x4)
host store integrity check passed; source saves unchanged
runs.launcher_save_failure_records: 4, all 'The authenticated host connection is unavailable' from the launchers' autosave scheduler (autosave was off); this harness revision did not record when; no pending recovery file was left and every later check passed. The harness now records the time and the preceding check of each.

failed_runs.cause: harness timeouts with four games on two cores; the waits were lengthened
harness: the field went busy during a walk out of the grass (Route 101 14,10); the walk now waits for the field and runs from a wild battle
harness: a step down was blocked at Route 101 (9,17); the walk now follows absolute waypoints round the rock
product bug KNOWN_ISSUES M6: the Players menu cut names to 13 characters before the friendship level, so 'Multi Friend 1..3' all read 'Multi Friend'; fixed (25 characters)

the battle went to recovery after 8 routed blocks with the processors overloaded (load 7.5 on 2 cores; cause not recorded); 640x360 windows and SDL_FRAMEBUFFER_ACCELERATION=0 cut each game from about 39% to 16% of a core
an enrollment failed and its cause was not kept; the harness now captures the enrollment error
stopped on purpose at 351 routed blocks (no failure) when the owner changed priorities; the games were ended by process id

harness: during slot 1's enrollment walk the field stayed busy for 45 s at Route 101 (10,11) without a battle menu; the game was closed before a picture was taken. The walk's field wait now saves a picture and the game's main callbacks when it gives up (field-stuck-N.png)

not_covered: Windows clients (Wine) and the 3D build in a 2v2
an interrupted 2v2 (host loss, disconnect, game closed mid-battle)
physical keyboard or controller input and clicks on the launcher windows
separate PCs, Wi-Fi or Internet (one machine over loopback)
